frozen_hypothesis: A direct natural-language cardinality request should favor outer SQL COUNT/SUM projection; a direct average request should favor AVG/ratio/named avg projection. Gate changes only where the original executable candidate violates the contract and an executable alternative matches. Train on original publisher TRAIN242 only; test on real original model VAL64 four disjoint TRAIN physical DBs.

train_reference_audit.note: These are warning flags, not verified erroneous publisher references. Rule is unsafe to impose as a universal hard constraint.

decision.reason: The frozen question→SQL operation cue has zero actionable disagreement and zero error discrimination in independent real same-model Qwen VAL64 (even with 13 covered questions). TRAIN242 original publisher SQL itself has three source-compatibility warnings. Full DEV500 reexecution would be wasteful.
decision.next_priority: Need an independent, higher-information semantic verifier (values, table/column/entity relationships, aggregate grain, or model-based candidate critique) with a separate truly unseen TRAIN DB/model evaluation. Do not add more keywords or change gate based on already-opened VAL64 results.
avoid: retraining or stronger model substitution without owner consent
claiming old 52-case oracle gap as a new gain

limitations: Validation is only 64 tasks across four separate source TRAIN physical databases; zero triggers does not disprove semantic reranking generally.
VAL64 compared existing heterogeneous direct and guarded Qwen pipeline results, not an actual frozen K8 generated candidate set.
The rule addresses only cardinality and average operation intent; question/table/value semantic mismatch and multi-hop relation errors are not covered.
Some publisher reference SQL may not satisfy natural-language intent; training-reference contract violations are unadjudicated flags.
